A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CGS-GAN and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendix A.1–A.9. v3 retains this material and adds funding acknowledgments and a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: v2 reports original human-head synthesis experiments, including FID scores, resource measurements, ablations, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, failure cases, and contrastive-loss analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A.2 retain the same generator architecture, multi-view regularization, discriminator conditioning, removal of generator view-conditioning, and random-background augmentation.

E1.justification: Both versions use FFHQ and FFHQ-Clean for human-head synthesis, with the same viewpoint coverage and explicit 3D environment demonstrations. No additional dataset, task, or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Section 5 retains GSGAN and GGHead as comparators. Appendix A.4 retains EG3D, Mimic3D, and Gaussian Shell Maps in the same comparison.

E3.justification: The FID/FID3D procedures, 50,000-image evaluations, resolutions, training settings, and performance-measurement protocols remain unchanged. The checklist introduces no revised experimental design.

E4.justification: The multi-view-count, background, and dataset-rebalancing analyses are retained. Appendix A.6 failure cases and A.7 contrastive-loss analysis also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly states that resource costs prevented repeated training of the proposed and comparison models. This adds repeated-run information absent from v2; no error bars, significance tests, or additional runs are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values and rankings. For example, CGS-GAN's FFHQC FIDs remain 4.53, 5.25, and 7.8 at 512², 1024², and 2048². The qualitative examples and contrastive-loss curve are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1) and its mathematical discussion in Appendix A.7 are unchanged. The checklist merely confirms the absence of theoretical results or proofs; none are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning 3D consistency, stable training, efficient high-resolution generation, background augmentation, and FFHQC curation.

C2.justification: The checklist newly acknowledges the resource limitation preventing repeated training. Item 11 also dismisses safeguard-related risks because the data are public, creating tension with the misuse concerns retained in Appendix A.3. Existing technical interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Checklist items 5 and 12 add statements about reviewer access to code, planned public code with reproduction instructions, and FFHQ's CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. Existing implementation and checkpoint disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish completed public code release.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 38 cited research works are retained. Bibliography reflow around the new acknowledgments does not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds acknowledgments and funding information, appends the NeurIPS checklist, and replaces the preprint footer with conference information. The main narrative, section ordering, and original appendix prose remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: All 17 figures and three tables retain their content and structure. The funding paragraph reflows the references, appendix spacing and page breaks change slightly, and formatted checklist pages are appended.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves transparency by explicitly disclosing the lack of repeated training and adding funding, licensing, and code-access information. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. These gains are limited by the new safeguards answer's tension with Appendix A.3's existing misuse discussion.
